source: RMC-BestFit/src/RMC.BestFit/Estimation/GeneralizedMethodOfMoments.cs (the delegate constructor, C# 143, and the three delegates it takes) @ c2e6192
reference: RMC.BestFit @ c2e6192. Runs corehydro::numerics::support::run_callback (core/include/corehydro/numerics/support/callback_runner.hpp), group "gmm", method "fit", against the delegates named by `construct.callback` (the moment conditions), `construct.jacobian` and `construct.penalty` -- each a function the four runners write themselves as a native closure (a C++ lambda, an R closure, a Python function, a C# delegate), so every case crosses the real host-language boundary. This is upstream's OWN API: GeneralizedMethodOfMoments has TWO constructors, one taking an IGMMModel (C# 106) and one taking these delegates directly (C# 143), and `IGMMModel` has exactly one implementation -- Bulletin17CDistribution -- so until this group existed the packages could fit an LP3 flood-frequency model by GMM and nothing else. EVERY expected value here is EMITTER-READ: no upstream test fits this model, so the oracle is the real RMC.BestFit GeneralizedMethodOfMoments driven by tools/oracle_emitter with the equivalent C# delegates, never a value computed by this repo's own C++. Every catalog callback is built from + - * / alone, with each summation written as an explicit loop rather than any language's sum(), mean() or Average(): R's sum() and mean() accumulate in extended precision where C++, Python and C# accumulate in double, and one differing bit moves a fitted parameter. THE MODEL is the just-identified two-parameter method-of-moments fit of a Normal -- theta = (mu, sigma2), g = [mean(x - mu), mean((x - mu)^2 - sigma2)] -- chosen because its GMM optimum has a CLOSED FORM: q = p makes g(theta-hat) = 0 attainable, and the unique root is the sample mean (4.95) and the population variance (0.165) of the eight observations. So the parameter assertions are checkable arithmetic, not a regression against whatever the optimizer happened to return. j_stat is NOT asserted anywhere in this file, deliberately: on a just-identified fit the moment residual covariance V = S - D(D'S^-1 D)^-1 D' is THEORETICALLY ZERO, so g' V^-1 g is whatever inverting a numerically singular matrix happens to give. Measured on this exact problem across the four optimizers -- all converging to the same parameters to 1e-9 -- it is -1.3e-09, 8.6e+19, -7.7e-15 and 0.126, and under NelderMead it THROWS outright from R and Python (where callback/gmm.hpp reports NaN rather than failing an otherwise exact fit) while returning a number from the C++ fixture runner, whose compiled callback contracts `a * a - theta` into an FMA. fixtures/estimation/gmm_bulletin17c_smoke.json's |J| < 1e-3 check holds only because its far messier real-data V carries real noise; on this deliberately clean synthetic problem any bound would be a fiction. j_stat_pval is NaN because the degrees of freedom q - p = 0: a just-identified fit has no over-identifying restriction left over to test its own specification with. That is correct, not a defect (see docs/upstream-csharp-issues.md). THE OVER-IDENTIFIED CASE (over_identified_three_moments, q = 3 > p = 2 via Mom_NormalThreeMoments) exists because it is the only reachable route to a NON-ZERO degrees of freedom on this surface -- Bulletin 17C is structurally just-identified -- and so the only case whose p-value comes from the chi-squared branch of PostProcess() rather than the structural NaN. It does NOT rescue j_stat, and the measurement is worth recording rather than hiding: the ported estimator computes J as g' V^-1 g, and V = S - D(D'S^-1 D)^-1 D' has rank exactly q - p for ANY q and p, so V is singular by construction whether the fit is just-identified or not; over-identifying only moves the rank from 0 to 1. What the inverse of that singular matrix amplifies is the optimizer's first-order-condition residual, which is a tolerance (1e-8), not a rounding error, so the result differs by far more than any tolerance worth writing: measured on THIS case, the real C# library returns J = 214.59276580810547 with a p-value of 0 while the shared C++ core returns J = -129.458513140678 with a p-value of 1, from parameters that agree to 2e-11; across the four optimizers the core alone spans -129.46, 1.2e+08, 1268.6 and 3.8e+06. So j_stat and j_stat_pval are unasserted in this case too -- with NO oracle_skip and NO loosened tolerance, because there is no honest value to loosen TOWARDS. What IS pinned here is everything the case was added to reach: degree_of_freedom = 1, the q = 3 probe agreeing with the declared number_of_moment_conditions, and the parameters/standard errors/covariance of a genuine over-identified sandwich (a 3 x 2 Jacobian against a 3 x 3 weighting matrix), none of which any other case in the file exercises. THE CUBIC-JACOBIAN CASE (analytic_jacobian_cubic, via Mom_NormalFourthMoment and Jac_NormalFourthMoment) exists because analytic_jacobian does NOT discriminate and was for a while described as though it did. Mom_NormalMeanVariance is quadratic in mu and linear in sigma2, so its Jacobian is linear, and a central difference computes a linear derivative EXACTLY: discarding the jacobian delegate's return entirely moves that case's standard_error[0] by 5.4e-13 against a pinned rel 1e-7, which is to say every assertion in it passes bit for bit with the delegate ignored. Matching the FOURTH central moment instead makes dg2/dsigma = -1200 t^3 cubic, and a central difference of a cubic derivative carries an h^2/6 f''' truncation error that does not vanish. The eight observations are rescaled by 1/100 for the same reason the Task 5 HMC gradient fixture tuned its quartic coefficient: the ported step is h = 1e-4 (|theta| + 1), so the error relative to the derivative is about (h / sigma)^2, and a fitted sigma of 0.00404 turns it into something a tolerance can see. MEASURED on that case: ignoring the delegate moves standard_error[1] by 6.18e-04 relative (6182 times its 1e-7 tolerance), covariance[0,1] by 6.18e-04 and covariance[1,1] by 1.24e-03 (12360 times). The fitted PARAMETERS still do not discriminate -- both Jacobians point downhill to the same root, which is why the discriminating assertions are the sandwich ones and the case says so assertion by assertion. Tolerances follow fixtures/README.md's policy: optimizer-dependent parameters rel 1e-8, finite-difference-sensitive standard_error/covariance/correlation rel 1e-7. The result layout (parameter[j] / standard_error[j] / covariance[i,j] / correlation[i,j] / the J-statistic and bookkeeping scalars, dims = {p, p}) is documented in core/include/corehydro/numerics/support/callback/gmm.hpp; the `named` assertions below read it by label rather than by an index that shifts with the parameter count.

callbacks.Mom_NormalMeanVariance: moment_conditions(parameters) -> (g, s) with g = [mean(x - mu), mean((x - mu)^2 - sigma2)] and s = the 2 x 2 covariance of those two contributions, over x = [4.1, 5.2, 4.8, 5.5, 4.9, 5.1, 5.3, 4.7]; every sum an explicit loop  [corehydro addition, upstream's `(Vector G, Matrix S) MomentConditionFunction(double[])` shape: the textbook just-identified method-of-moments fit of a Normal, whose root is the sample mean and the population variance]
callbacks.Mom_NormalThreeMoments: moment_conditions(parameters) -> (g, s) with g = [mean(x - mu), mean((x - mu)^2 - sigma2), mean((x - mu)^3)] and s = the 3 x 3 covariance of those three contributions, over the same eight observations; every sum an explicit loop  [corehydro addition, the same `MomentConditionFunction` shape: the OVER-IDENTIFIED companion of Mom_NormalMeanVariance. The third central moment is zero for a Normal, so adding it as a moment condition leaves the model unchanged and makes q = 3 > p = 2, DegreeOfFreedom = 1. This is the only case in the file that reaches the chi-squared p-value branch of PostProcess(), and the only one for which OneStep is refused by the estimator]
callbacks.Mom_NormalFourthMoment: moment_conditions(parameters) -> (g, s) with theta = (mu, sigma), g = [mean(x - mu), mean(u^4) - 3 t^4] where u = 100 (x - mu) and t = 100 sigma, and s = the 2 x 2 covariance of those two contributions, over x = [0.041, 0.052, 0.048, 0.055, 0.049, 0.051, 0.053, 0.047]; every sum an explicit loop  [corehydro addition, the same `MomentConditionFunction` shape: the CUBIC-JACOBIAN companion of Mom_NormalMeanVariance. Matching the FOURTH central moment of a Normal, E[(x - mu)^4] = 3 sigma^4, makes dg2/dsigma = -1200 t^3 cubic in the parameter, where every other member of this catalog has a Jacobian linear in it. The eight observations are the ones above with the decimal point moved two places, which puts the fitted sigma (0.00404) well below the ported numerical Jacobian's step h = 1e-4 (|theta| + 1); the factors of 100 write the fourth-moment condition on the same order of magnitude as the first, which GMM is invariant to because W = S^-1 absorbs a constant rescaling of a moment condition]
callbacks.Jac_NormalMeanVariance: jacobian(parameters) -> the analytic 2 x 2 dg/dtheta of Mom_NormalMeanVariance, one ROW per moment condition: [[-1, 0], [-2 mean(x - mu), -1]]  [corehydro addition, upstream's `double[,] JacobianFunction(double[])` shape: replaces the ported bounds-aware finite-difference Jacobian. Note that it does not DISCRIMINATE -- the Jacobian it returns is linear in theta, so the central difference it replaces computes the same matrix; Jac_NormalFourthMoment is the one that does]
callbacks.Jac_NormalFourthMoment: jacobian(parameters) -> the analytic 2 x 2 dg/dtheta of Mom_NormalFourthMoment, one ROW per moment condition: [[-1, 0], [-400 mean(u^3), -1200 t^3]]  [corehydro addition, the same `JacobianFunction` shape: the discriminating one. Its second row is cubic in theta, so the ported central difference carries an h^2/6 f''' truncation error rather than reproducing it exactly, and the fitted standard errors move by 6.2e-04 relative when the delegate's return is discarded]
callbacks.Pen_SigmaTowardsOne: penalty(parameters) -> 0.5 * (sigma2 - 1)^2  [corehydro addition, upstream's `double PenaltyFunction(double[])` shape: a ridge penalty carrying its own 1/2, as the half-quadratic convention in Q() expects. It pulls sigma2 away from the closed-form 0.165 and towards 1, which is what makes this case an oracle for the delegate being reached at all rather than a repeat of the first]
